How it works

The stack

Every compound you are running, on one clock

One vial, several peptides. Put in what the vial actually holds of each, the amounts, not a ratio, and every dose is split the same way. The curve uses the slowest component, because that is what decides when the mixture reaches steady state, and each component is drawn on its own on the Levels screen.

The published library will always be behind what people actually run. Add anything with its own numbers, it will be marked as yours everywhere it appears, and in the record, so nobody mistakes it for published data.

Everything at once

Each compound against its own steady-state peak, different molecules are not comparable in mg

Solve the mix

Every diluent volume from 0.5 to 5.0 mL, scored on where the plunger actually lands

The other calculators hand you a number like 8.33 units and stop. No barrel has a 0.33 tick. This solver rounds to the tick you can actually hit, reports the dose that really leaves the needle, and searches every diluent volume for the one that lands the plunger on a whole number.

Lean share of loss
,
Body fat from the US Navy circumference equations; fat mass and fat-free mass split from it at both ends of the run. Trials of GLP-1 therapy have repeatedly found roughly a quarter to 40% of total weight lost is lean tissue. Every other tracker shows you one line, pounds, which cannot tell those two apart.

Which dose gets the credit

Attribution by modeled exposure, not by the nearest calendar entry

A reading taken on Saturday does not belong to Saturday. It belongs to whichever dose was actually driving your blood level at that moment, and with a 5-day half-life that is usually not the most recent one. This is the bug users report in the biggest app in the category. Here it is done properly: every reading is attributed to the dose contributing the largest share of modeled concentration at that instant.
